rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may make the Prophet forget a revelation by abrogating it, or display the Quran's power over even the greatest creature as a forgotten verse is later recalled.
rows.anchor: أن تنساه لأنه نسخه , أو لتظهر عظمته في أن أعظم الخلق يغلبه القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God continuously knows public recitation and whatever is concealed, with the explicit pair showing both are equally within His knowledge.
rows.anchor: يعلمه مطلقا لا بقيد كونه جهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the Prophet prepared, gentle, guided, and at ease in preserving and reflecting on revelation and in all easy ways.
rows.anchor: نجعلك أنت مهيأ مسهلا ملينا موفقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says God makes the Prophet himself easy because he is naturally disposed to love ease, rather than merely making ease available to him.
rows.anchor: ونيسر لك , لأنه هو مطبوع على حبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying that everyone is facilitated toward what they were created for supports the interpretation of divine facilitation.
rows.anchor: قوله : ( كل ميسر لما خلق له )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must remind everyone in every circumstance, with compassion, as a skilled physician treats patients and with authorization like a student receiving a teacher's approval.
rows.anchor: قد صار كالطبيب الحاذق في علاج المرضى فيقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional phrasing means remind whenever benefit can be hoped for; since people cannot know the unseen, the Prophet should not despair or stop calling anyone.
rows.anchor: لا يقطع بعدم نفع أحد بل لا يزال على رجاء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commands to turn away from rejecters concern avoiding grief and self-torment over them, not abandoning reminder.
rows.anchor: إنما هو بالإعراض عن الحزن عليه ومن تقطيع النفس لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People divide into those who accept treatment and those who do not; God has always known each person's outcome but leaves them unidentified as a trial and proof against them.
rows.anchor: عالم بكل من القسمين جملة وأفرادا على التعيين ولم يزل عالما بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with even an innate measure of fear will heed the reminder, because fear leads to every good and belongs to the felicitous.
rows.anchor: في جبلته نوع خشية , وهو السعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love for God is shown by following, while aversion is shown by avoiding the reminder, refusing it, and innovating against it.
rows.anchor: وعلامة الحب الاقتداء , وعلامة البغض التجنب والانتهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched person makes himself resist the reminder from the noblest messenger and is absolutely wretched because he opposes the greatest messenger and does not fear.
rows.anchor: لأنه خالف أشرف الرسل فهو لا يخشى فكان أشقى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers in Muhammad are nobler than those who believed in earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: من آمن به أشرف ممن آمن بمن قبله من الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched person plunges heart and body into the greatest fire, understood as Hell's lowest level because he is hard-hearted through ignorance, blind imitation, or arrogant defiance.
rows.anchor: أعظم الطبقات وهي السفلى لأنه ليس في طبعه أن يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the greatest fire is the afterlife fire, seventy times greater than the fire of the intermediate realm and the present world.
rows.anchor: نار الأخرى فإنها أعظم من نار البرزخ وأعظم من نار الدنيا بسبعين جزءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses ellipsis by correspondence: fear and happiness in the first group imply the omitted hard-heartedness and misery of the second, while the second group's cause and outcome imply the first group's opposites.
rows.anchor: ذكر الثمرة في الأول وهي الخشية دليلا على حذف ضدها من الثاني

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Mulawi says Quranic eloquence pairs cause and outcome across passages, avoiding repetition; he illustrates decree, execution, and allocation through the planning and operation of a waterwheel.
rows.anchor: قال الملوي : ولا شك أن القرآن العظيم على أحسن ما يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word then marks the great interval or degree between enduring the fire and the bewildering state between death and life, whose full severity only God knows.
rows.anchor: فأشار إلى ذلك بالتعبير بأداة التراخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned neither die in the fire, however long it lasts, nor live a beneficial life because they were not purified, believed, or prayed.
rows.anchor: حياة تنفعه لأنه ما تزكى فلا صدق ولا صلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True purification combines abandoning prohibitions and pursuing commands through disciplined worship and struggle after the warning against ruin.
rows.anchor: فجمع الاجتناب والاجتلاب بالتزكية بالتبتل بالأبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prosperity means attaining every desired good; purification cleanses belief, character, speech, deeds, and wealth while growing inward and outward acts and charity.
rows.anchor: تطهيرها من فاسد الاعتقادات والأخلاق والأقوال والأفعال والأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification is the glorification commanded at the sura's opening and the good actions that follow from it.
rows.anchor: وذلك هو التسبيخ الذي أمر به أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's attributes of beneficence delights the inner self and appears outwardly in words; recalling the name also evokes its named referent.
rows.anchor: إذا ذكر الصفة سر بها فأفاض باطنه على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ritual prayer is the greatest bodily worship, as almsgiving is the greatest worship of wealth, and remembrance and prayer protect from vanity and its defects.
rows.anchor: الصلاة الشرعية لأنها أعظم الذكر , فهي أعظم عبادات البدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purification, remembrance, and prayer reprise the opening's divine traits: removing defects and acquiring perfections; this paired ellipsis links prayer with escape from the greatest fire.
rows.anchor: وكان متخلقا بما ذكر من أخلاق الله في أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording can include fitr almsgiving, Eid takbirs, and Eid prayer despite the sura being Meccan, since wording is general and revelation may precede a ruling.
rows.anchor: والآية صالحة لإرادة زكاة الفطر وتكبيرات العيد وصلاته

rows.speaker: الرازي في اللوامع
rows.claim: Al-Razi says fitr almsgiving precedes Eid prayer; Ibn Masud recited this verse after saying may God show mercy to one who gives charity then prays.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : وتقدم زكاة الفطر على صلاة العيد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud linked the verse to giving charity and then praying, although the sura is Meccan and the ruling came later.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه يقول : رحم الله أمرأ تصدق ثم صلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People prefer the low, transient present world because its immediacy captivates sense-bound creatures and consumes time meant for remembrance and purification.
rows.anchor: أي الدنية بالفناء الحاضرة , مع أنها شر وفانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly attachment produces bodily appetites and love of wealth that lead to evil deeds.
rows.anchor: في داء القبقب وهو البطن , والدبدب وهو الفرج , وحب المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is the goal of creation and wiser than a purposeless world; its unclouded pleasure is better and permanently enduring, incomparable to what passes.
rows.anchor: نعيم الآخرة دائم لا انقطاع له أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical pairing leaves rejecting the afterlife implicit after mention of worldly preference, then uses the afterlife's goodness and permanence to imply the world's opposite; it deters from the base and attracts to the lasting.
rows.anchor: والمستلذات الوهمية , والآية من الاحتباك :

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar instructed Nafi to act similarly and said the verse was revealed about this practice.
rows.anchor: وزاد البغوي أن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما كان يأمر نافعا رضي الله عنه بنحو ما قال ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar reports from Awf ibn Malik that the Prophet ordered fitr almsgiving before Eid prayer and recited this verse; the chain's Kathir ibn Abd Allah was judged hasan by al-Tirmidhi but weakened by others.
rows.anchor: وروى البزار : ( عن عوف بن مالك الأشجعي رضي الله تعالى عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يأمر بزكاة الفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura's Meccan date does not prevent a later ruling, as the verse about the sanctuary's inviolability preceded its effect at the conquest.
rows.anchor: السورة مكية , وظهر أثر الحل يوم الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refers to the great admonition of glorification, purification, remembrance, prayer, and turning from the world toward the afterlife; it gathers all good and belongs to every revealed law, so its aim cannot be abrogated.
rows.anchor: أي الوعظ العظيم بالتسبيح الذي ذكر في هذه السور وما تأثر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran preserves unsurpassed eloquence, genres of poetry, legal limits, and unseen knowledge, surpassing poets and soothsayers and showing Muhammad follows earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: فإن القرآن جمع المديح الفائق والنسيب الرقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's scrolls come first because they are closer to admonition, as the report of Abu Dharr indicates; Moses' book comes last because it chiefly contains laws and fewer admonitions.
rows.anchor: قدمه لأن صحفه أقرب إلى الوعظ كما نطق به حديث أبي ذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order also follows the prophets' historical existence and precedence in merit; Moses' scrolls contain severe warnings and the glad tidings of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ذكر النبيين عليهما الصلاة والسلام على الأصل في ترتيب الوجود والأفضلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ending with purification returns to the beginning's glorification and soul-cleansing; God does not leave creation without guidance or create them purposelessly.
rows.anchor: وكان في إتيانه والتذكير به إعلام بأن الله تعالى لم يهمل الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura explains the end of Sabbih by affirming the afterlife, beginning with the Overwhelming Event, describing the fates of the pious and wicked, and demonstrating God's power over it.
rows.anchor: من تنزيه الله سبحانه وتعالى عن العبث بإثبات الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Ghashiya points to the strongest sign of the sura's purpose; he seeks refuge from an obscured heart and insight and deeds that bring calamity.
rows.anchor: نعوذ بالله من القلب الغاشي والبصيرة الغاشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura explains the end of Sabbih by affirming the afterlife, beginning with the Overwhelming Event, describing the fates of the pious and wicked, and demonstrating God's power over it.
rows.anchor: من تنزيه الله سبحانه وتعالى عن العبث بإثبات الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Ghashiya points to the strongest sign of the sura's purpose; he seeks refuge from an obscured heart and insight and deeds that bring calamity.
rows.anchor: نعوذ بالله من القلب الغاشي والبصيرة الغاشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura follows the warning against worldly preference with a warning against turning from purification through any route other than the prophets' method.
rows.anchor: رهب أول هذه من الإعراض عن ذلك مرة , ومن التزكي بغير منهاج الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addresses the Prophet clearly and honors him by asking whether the account of the Overwhelming Event reached him.
rows.anchor: أي جاءك وكان لك وواجهك على وجه الوضوح يا أعظم خلقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghashiya is the Resurrection, which covers people with terrible calamities, hardships, warnings, and prohibitions, since covering describes something disliked.
rows.anchor: القيامة التي تغشي الناس بدواهيها وشدائدها العظمى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr explains the coherence: after divine transcendence, the question magnifies Resurrection; the passage gives the damned's ordeal, contrasts the blessed, adduces created signs, and commands reminder when signs failed to persuade.
rows.anchor: أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تقدم تنزيهه سبحانه عما توهم الظالمون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In al-Awfi's report from Ibn Abbas, the condemned work in Hell, hauling chains and shackles and enduring fire because they neglected deeds in worldly life; their labor is exhausting and futile.
rows.anchor: هذه رواية العوفي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما , وذلك لأنهم لم يخشوا الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Alternatively, Ibn Abbas as transmitted by Ata refers to people who exhausted themselves in worldly practices outside Islam, such as monks after abrogation and philosophical Sufi heretics.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في رواية عطاء عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative reading, faces is the subject and that day is its predicate, with the laboring and exhaustion describing their worldly condition.
rows.anchor: بأن يكون ( وجوه ) مبتدأ و ( يومئذ ) خبره

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr, Yaqub, and Abu Bakr from Asim read tasla passively, emphasizing that the disliked punishment is imposed upon the sufferers.
rows.anchor: في قراءة أبي عمرو ويعقوب وأبي بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common active reading says the people themselves enter and immerse themselves in the fire, showing extreme humiliation.
rows.anchor: والمعنى على قراءة الجماعة بالبناء للفاعل : تدخل وتباشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is intensely hot because they acted in ignorance against their prophets' limits and heedlessness left no opening for mercy.
rows.anchor: متناهية في الحر لأنها عملت بالجهل على خلاف ما حده لها نبيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boiling spring reaches its extreme heat: when brought near it burns facial flesh, and when drunk it cuts the intestines, matching their worldly indulgence in passion.
rows.anchor: بلغت غايتها في الحر فنضجت غاية النضج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their only food is the foul, poisonous, thorny dry shibriq called dhari; a camel eats it only when wet and avoids it once dry.
rows.anchor: شوك ترعاه الإبل ما دام رطبا

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus gives dhari as shibriq or its dry form, and also records descriptions of a bitter, foul Hell plant and a foul sea-cast plant.
rows.anchor: وقال في القاموس : والضريع كأمير : الشبرق أو يبيسه أو نبات رطبه يسمى شبرقا

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: Al-Harawi and Abd al-Haqq define dhari as the known thorny Hijazi plant called shibriq while fresh and dhari when dry.
rows.anchor: وقال الهروي في الغريبين وعبد الحق في الواعي : الضريع : الشبرق

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz's dictionary says dhari is dried wood, especially dry shibriq, or a green plant cast up by the sea.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز في ديوانه : الضريع : يبيس من يبيس الشجر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa describes it as forage that does not add fat or flesh to grazing animals and worsens their condition if eaten exclusively.
rows.anchor: أبو حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى : وهو مرعى لا تعقد عليه السائمة

rows.speaker: ابن الأثير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Athir says dhari is a large-thorned Hijazi plant and shibriq is edible fresh but called dhari when dry.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأثير في النهاية : الضريع هو نبت بالحجاز له شوك كبار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and Ikrima identify dhari as a low thorny plant called shibriq by Quraysh, named dhari when dry and their foulest food; al-Awfi transmits the same from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة وعكرمة : هو نبت ذو شوك لاطئ بالأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may be Hell's ghislin transformed after leaving the damned's bodies into the shape of dhari, or a metaphor for the worst existence without a specific plant intended.
rows.anchor: ولا يمتنع في قدرة الله سبحانه وتعالى أن يكون الغسلين إذا انفصل

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Mulawi says dhari is so named because its roughness, bitterness, and stench make the eater plead while eating it.
rows.anchor: قال الملوي : وسمي ضريعا لأن الإنسان يتضرع عند أكله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits from the Prophet that the damned's dhari is thorny fire, so it brings no nourishment or relief.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما مرفوعا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food neither fattens nor strengthens, nor fills them; it cannot preserve health or prevent wasting, so it fails both aims of food.
rows.anchor: أي فلا يشبتع ولا يقوي لأنه يلزم ما يسمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is mistaken to read the verse as denying some kinds of food while leaving food that does fatten or satisfy; that reverses the meaning.
rows.anchor: ومن جعل ذلك سفة الطعام أفسد المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who ate forbidden food and doubtful things corrupted their bodies and souls; philosophy, poetry, sorcery, and related pursuits darken hearts and lead to innovations.
rows.anchor: كانوا يأكلون الحرام الذي تنبت عليه لحومهم فيفسدها بفساده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired ellipsis makes the denial of fatness imply wasting and the denial of relief from hunger imply lack of satiety.
rows.anchor: نفي السمن أولا يدل على إثبات الهزال ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' faces are radiant, joyful, comfortable, and luxurious, unlike the exhausted faces because they disciplined themselves and endured hardship in the world.
rows.anchor: ذات بهجة وسرور تظهر عليها النعمة والنضرة والراحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are pleased with their afterlife efforts when they see the reward and wish they had devoted all their worldly work to them, though such work once felt burdensome.
rows.anchor: لما رأت من ثوابه تود أن جميع سعيها في الدنيا كان لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is high in location and rank, with trees and rooms, because its people turned from low things and raised their aims toward precious things.
rows.anchor: في المكان العالي والمكانة العالية والأشجار والغرف

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Raways from Yaqub read the phrase passively, which makes the negation more emphatic; the majority read it actively as address to the entrant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ورويس عن يعقوب بالبناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase excludes any vain speech, vain speaker, or word containing vanity by figurative attribution; only praise and glorification are heard, prompted by wonders and hearts freed from worldly appetites.
rows.anchor: لغو ما أو نفس تلغو أو كلمة ذات لغو على الإسناد المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After first removing disturbance, the description offers pleasures: a flowing spring supplies drink and improves the garden, whose plants and birds thrive; not every known garden has naturally running water.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس كل جنة مما نعرفه فيه ماء جار بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular spring is generic and immensely abundant, never ceasing and reaching every part of the spacious garden and even its elevated rooms by God's power.
rows.anchor: وحد قوله المراد به الجنس الشامل للكثير مقابلة لعين أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many elevated couches mark royal status; the passive form and indeterminate adjective magnify their extraordinary height and show that God raises them from their natural lowered state.
rows.anchor: وبنى الاسم للمفعول للدلالة على أنه ليس له من ذاتها إلا الانخفاض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says their boards are gold inlaid with jewels; they rise before the owners arrive, lower for them to sit, then rise back to their places.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ألواحها من ذهب مكللة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cups have no handle, allowing people to pass and drink from any side; they are full and easy to reach.
rows.anchor: جمع كوب وهو إناء لا عروة له , فهو صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cushions are pillows for resting, set in rows and so numerous they resemble aligned hills.
rows.anchor: أي مساند يستندون إليها , جمع نمرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rugs are broad, thick-piled, luxurious, and widely spread among recreation places and gardens; this suits those who softened themselves to truth in worldly life.
rows.anchor: بسط عريضة كثيرة الوبر كأنها الرياض فاخرة ناضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke addresses deniers early in revelation, recalling obvious signs that establish resurrection and God's ability to create the described gardens, Hell, and their pleasures.
rows.anchor: فوبخهم بما يعصمهم من الزيغ عن العقائد الحقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs include both creatures capable of voluntary lowering and rising and fixed forms with different heights and surfaces, all displaying wondrous creation.
rows.anchor: مع تفاوته في جعل بعضها ذا اختيار في الخفض والرفع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan highlights the camel's exceptional usefulness: it eats any pasture, needs little water, tolerates long thirst, and combines great size, strength, and usefulness.
rows.anchor: مع أكلها لكل مرعى واجتزائها بأيسر شيء لا سيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel is a singular and especially crafted animal, created to carry heavy loads far away, kneel and rise without help, obey its handler, and cross deserts, making it evidence of intentional power.
rows.anchor: خلقها لجر الأثقال إلى البلاد النائية فجعلها عظيمة باركة للحمل

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi says camels are singled out because they show dispersed signs in animals, the most finely crafted composites, and are the most astonishing creature familiar to Arabs.
rows.anchor: قال البيضاوي : ولذلك خصت بالذكر لبيان الآيات المنبثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel's yielding, endurance, movement to pleasant sound, and response to kneeling and rising echo the garden's flowing spring, lowered and raised couches, cups, cushions, and spread rugs.
rows.anchor: ولعله مثل العين الجارية وقربها بدرها , والسرر المرفوعة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says how asks about the camel's condition and is governed by created; when a verb is governed by an interrogative, the question is no longer literal.
rows.anchor: و { كيف } سؤال عن حال والعامل فيه { خلقت * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel demonstrates divine action by choice against naturalism, so the sky follows as another sign that counters those who claim nature acts by itself.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه وتعالى هذا المخلوق المفرد الذي هو أدل ما يكون على هذا القول بالطبيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the vast, weighty sky without pillars and filled it with celestial wonders; this proves power to make high gardens and raised couches through choice, not nature.
rows.anchor: حصل بأيسر أمر رفعها من الذي خلقها بلا عمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God set mountains firmly high without natural necessity; they provide water and trees, stabilize the earth, and regularize celestial cycles and the calendar, which requires one sovereign creator.
rows.anchor: وبها مع ذلك ثبتت الأرض وحفظت من الميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spread the broad, ornamented earth into an easy bed; its varied vegetation shows purposeful creation and God's capacity to spread paradise rugs.
rows.anchor: اتفق بسطها من باسطها حتى صارت مهادا موضوعا يمشي عليه بغاية السهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wonders of heavenly and earthly creations prove God's power over everything, including resurrection and all promised forms of reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: فدل على كمال قدرته - على البعث وعلى كل ما ذكر أنه يفعله في الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs also symbolize the inward person: the camel is the obedient soul, heaven the holy spirit, mountains stable intellect and knowledge, and earth the body and its organs.
rows.anchor: الإبل تشبه الأنفس المطمئنة الذلولة المطيعة المناقدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should remind anyone likely to benefit, awakening innate knowledge in creation so people recognize the Creator's power and the resurrection; their failure to reflect should not trouble him.
rows.anchor: كل من يرجى تذكره وانتفاعه بالتذكير يا أشرف خخلقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As this is an early Meccan sura when the Prophet was commanded to pardon, he is only a reminder and not an enforcer; he will soon gain authority over others.
rows.anchor: وكان مأمورا إذ ذاك بالصفح قال : { إنما أنت مذكر

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai reads the word with sin, preserving its original pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقرأها الكسائي بالسين على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception describes a person who forces his pure nature toward rejection and persists in disbelief; God punishes him with the greatest punishment because he rejected the Prophet.
rows.anchor: كلف نفسه المطمئنة وفطرته الأولى المستقيمة للإعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the exception is formally disconnected, it is phrased like a connected exception to indicate that their punishment from God results from denying the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولعله صوره وهو منقطع بصورة المتصل بالتعبير بأداته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the opening as ala with a lightened hamza and fatHa, treating it as an introductory particle rather than an exception.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ( ألا ) بالفتح والتخفيف على أنها استفتاحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception is connected: God gives the Prophet power over those who persist in disbelief, who are killed and then punished in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الاستثناء متصلا فيكون المعنى : أن من أصر على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest punishment means the punishment of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: العذاب الأكبر * } يعني عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite denial, everyone returns exclusively to God at death, resurrection, and gathering.
rows.anchor: رجوعهم وإن أبوا بالموت ثم بالبعث ثم بالحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After return, God alone accounts for every small and great deed; His power, freedom from injustice and purposelessness, and firm promises guarantee the reckoning.
rows.anchor: أي يوم القيامة على النقير والقطمير , وغير ذلك من كل صغير وكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura ends by linking back to its opening: the Overwhelming Event divides people between a home of humiliation and a home of safety.
rows.anchor: وذلك يكون في الغاشية يوم ينقسم الناس قسمين : في دار هوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fajr sura's purpose is to support the return and reckoning mentioned at the end of Ghashiya: dawn's emergence resembles sleepers returning from death-like sleep to daytime work for reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الاستدلال على آخر الغاشية الإياب والحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala depicts God gathering servants after dispersal through divine majesty, giving them clarifying guidance, and granting the chosen their gardens through mercy.
rows.anchor: جامع العباد بعد تمزيقهم بما له من العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People failed to infer from camels, sky, mountains, and earth—created for transport, water, shade, storage, and habitation—and failed to learn from earlier nations such as Ad.
rows.anchor: فالإبل لأثقالهم وانتقالهم , والسماء لسقيهم وإظلالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of Ad and God's watchfulness should make them heed the warning now rather than remember only when remembrance no longer helps.
rows.anchor: بالمرصاد } فيتذكرون حين لا ينفع التذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted oath's answer is that all will be raised, gathered, judged, and repaid; belief brings safety while denial brings punishment, confirmed by God's power over creation and punishment.
rows.anchor: ليبعثن كلهم صاغرين ثم ليحشرن ثم ليحاسبن فيجازى كل أحد بما عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iram can mean the people of Ad or their principal city, the name applied metonymically through their close association with its remarkable construction.
rows.anchor: أي أهلها وعمدتها , وأطلقها عليهم لشدة الملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city had unprecedented tall, pillar-supported buildings and remarkable facilities, fruit, water, scenery, and birds; the pronoun may refer to Ad as a tribe or Iram as a city.
rows.anchor: أي صاحبة { العماد * } أي البناء العالي الثابت بالأعمدة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the city's claimed qualities would be difficult or ordinarily impossible to match anywhere on earth.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : على أوصاف بعيد أو مستحيل عادة أن يكون في الأرض مثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Shaddad built a rival paradise in Aden over three hundred years, died before entering it, and his city vanished; Ibn Qilaba found it, and Kaab identified him as the foretold entrant, but the author's teacher says signs of fabrication are obvious.
rows.anchor: وآثار الوضع عليه لائحة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Some, including Ibn Abbas, apply all the descriptions to the tribe: the first Ad, named for ancestor Iram, were nomadic Arabs who lived in pillar-supported tents and were unmatched in strength and stature.
rows.anchor: وقال جماعة منهم ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : الأوصاف كلها للقبيلة وهم عاد الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion moves from Ad to the nearer and similar Thamud, who received gardens and crops but answered divine favor with disbelief and preferred blindness; their she-camel was a clear sign of power.
rows.anchor: ثنى بأقرب الأمم إليهم زمانا وأشبههم بهم شأنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud cut through rock in the Valley of al-Hijr or Wadi al-Qura and carved mountain houses as if defying time.
rows.anchor: نقبوا وقطعوا قطعا حقيقا كأنه عندهم كالواجب

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says Thamud were the first to carve mountains, rocks, and marble, and built 1,700 stone cities.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : قيل أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام ثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his soldiers are described as people of stakes, whose armies and possessions secured a seemingly unshakable sovereignty; their story also displays signs of power over resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي الذي ثبت ملكه تثبيت من يظن أنه لا يزول بالعساكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural description collectively covers Pharaoh, his army, Ad, Thamud, and their followers: they exceeded bounds in lands they ruled and spread unbelief and injustice as an imitated precedent.
rows.anchor: فرعون وجنوده وكل من ذكر هنا من الكفرة من عاد وثمود وأتباعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God poured worldly punishment on them—drowning, earthquakes, and other forms—like a whip in force, speed, adhesion, and encompassing, with the word also associated with mixture and braided lashes.
rows.anchor: وأصله الخلط , وإنما سمي هذا الجلد المضفور الذي يضرب به
